title: Transport of ordinary base change across a source scheme isomorphism
statement: Let P,U,S,T be quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, f:P→S and f′:U→S be qcqs morphisms, e:U≅P satisfy e.hom followed by f equals f′, and g:T→S be any morphism. Choose right adjoints a,b,d,b′ with adjunctions to the canonical lifted direct images of f,f′, pullback(f,g)→T and pullback(f′,g)→T, respectively. Suppose ordinary base change for f′ along g is invertible on every object of D_QCoh(U). Let r:pullback(f′,g)→pullback(f,g) satisfy r followed by the projection to P equals the projection to U followed by e.hom, and r followed by the projection to T equals the projection to T. Then ordinary base change for f along g is invertible on every object of D_QCoh(P). Schemes, fibre products, derived categories, pullback, direct image, the canonical lifted qcqs direct image and ordinary base change are as in the cited dependency nodes.

proof.text: Construct the inverse of r by pullback.lift with components pullback.fst(f,g) followed by e.inv and pullback.snd(f,g). The commutativity follows from he and the original pullback condition. Pullback hom ext and the two projection equations show both composites are identities. This gives the explicit isomorphism er with hom r.

For E in D_QCoh(P), set N to derivedPullback(e.hom)(E). Apply the first conjunct of [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh] to equip N with its quasi-coherent-cohomology property. Construct z:L(pullback.fst(fprime,g))(N) isomorphic to Lr L(pullback.fst(f,g))(E) from the selected composition comparisons, equality transport along hr1 inverse, and the inverse composition comparison.

Apply [lem-pc-derived-base-change-source-iso] to the original fibre-product square, source isomorphisms e and er, identity coefficient arrow on L(pullback.fst(f,g))(E), identity alpha and beta, and coefficient arrow z.hom. Its coefficient equation follows by functor map_id and associativity. It gives endpoint isomorphisms a0 and b0 and an equality between the old base-change map followed by b0.hom and a0.hom followed by the transported base-change map and the direct image of z.hom.

Use he and hr2 to identify the transported comparison with the assumed invertible comparison hbeta at N; eliminate these equalities before applying hbeta to avoid dependent rewriting of the square proof. The image of z.hom and a0.hom are isomorphisms, so the comparison equation implies the original map followed by b0.hom is an isomorphism. Cancel b0.hom using isIso_comp_right_iff and cancel the direct image of the identity coefficient arrow using map_id.
